references.text: The continuation of God's speech about hiding His face because of the people's sin and idolatry
God repeats that He will hide His face from them because of their unfaithfulness
Isaiah speaks of the Lord hiding His face from the house of Jacob
Sin separates the people from God and causes Him to hide His face
God hides His face and hands the people over to their sins
Ezekiel explains that God hid His face from Israel because of their impurity and transgressions
Hosea prophesies that God will return to His place until the people acknowledge their guilt
Micah speaks of God hiding His face because of evil deeds
The Lord's wrath burns against Israel, and He hands them over to their enemies, as warned in Deuteronomy
David laments that God hid His face and he was terrified
The psalmist asks why God hides His face and forgets their distress
When God hides His face, the creatures are terrified
